ecomassistant.title: EcomAssistant
ecomassistant.summary: An AI WhatsApp agent that automatically confirms COD orders, follows up on unanswered ones, and answers customer questions in Derja, French, and Arabic — including voice notes and product photos.
ecomassistant.overview: Algerian e-commerce runs almost entirely on Cash on Delivery, and failed deliveries are the industry's biggest cost driver — most of them caused by orders that were never confirmed or forgotten by dispatch day. EcomAssistant automates the whole confirmation conversation on the merchant's own WhatsApp number.
ecomassistant.challenge: Merchants confirm orders manually over WhatsApp or phone, so anything ordered after hours goes unanswered. Customers who send Derja voice notes or ask product questions before committing often get no reply. The mix of languages makes automated replies hard to get right.
ecomassistant.solution: A SaaS that plugs into a store's Shopify via OAuth, then uses Google Gemini to interpret replies in Derda, French, and Arabic — text, voice notes, and product photos — and acts through a fixed tool registry for order lookup, shipment creation, and product search. BullMQ queues handle retries and background jobs so no order is ever lost.
results: Order confirmation went from manual to fully automatic across three languages
Failed deliveries dropped as unanswered orders are followed up before dispatch
Merchants manage everything from one dashboard instead of juggling separate tools

nktex.title: NKTex
nktex.summary: A React Native stock-counting app for a textile company where workers submit weekly counts per location and the admin tracks totals and generates a print-ready PDF production report.
nktex.overview: NKTex's weekly stock counts were collected on paper and aggregated by hand. Summing counts from multiple locations took hours, there was no quick view of totals versus maximum quantities, and production planning was guesswork.
nktex.challenge: Paper counts from multiple locations had to be re-entered and summed by hand. Workers shared devices and could not handle complex auth flows. The admin needed an instant picture of what to produce next, but production reports took too long to assemble.
nktex.solution: A React Native (Expo) app with custom profile-based auth for shared devices, weekly stock entries with database-level upsert guarantees, a Supabase backend with RLS scoping workers to their location, and a one-tap PDF report that auto-selects items needing production.
results: Weekly paper counting became a few minutes on a phone
The production report tells the team exactly what to produce next
Stock totals are visible in real time instead of at month's end

dentora.title: Dentora PMS
dentora.summary: A full-stack dental practice management system — patient records, scheduling, billing, stock, staff payroll, and a patient portal — across four apps in a pnpm monorepo.
dentora.overview: Dental clinics in Algeria manage patients, appointments, billing, stock, and staff through paper records, spreadsheets, and phone calls. There is no integrated system that handles the full practice workflow while respecting Algerian data protection law.
dentora.challenge: Paper-based records are slow to search and impossible to audit. Appointment scheduling relies on phone calls with frequent double-bookings. Billing is manual, stock tracking is ad-hoc, and there is no patient portal. Compliance with data protection law 18-07 requires field-level encryption for patient data.
dentora.solution: A pnpm monorepo with four apps — public marketing site, staff admin SPA, patient portal, and Express API — sharing contracts, i18n, UI components, and config packages. Patient PII is encrypted with AES-256-GCM via custom Prisma middleware, and the admin and portal apps are PWAs with offline support for low-connectivity environments.
results: Clinic operations consolidated into one system instead of scattered tools
Patient data encrypted at rest, compliant with Algerian law 18-07
Staff can work offline in low-connectivity environments via PWA

groundwork.title: Groundwork
groundwork.summary: A complete coffee shop system in one monorepo — customer ordering site, staff admin with live SSE order queue, and a type-safe backend that re-prices every order server-side.
groundwork.overview: A single coffee shop juggles ordering, the kitchen queue, inventory, loyalty, and staff across paper tickets, a spreadsheet, and memory. Customers can't order ahead, baristas can't see the live queue, and stock runs out mid-service.
groundwork.challenge: Three apps can drift apart — a schema change in one place silently breaks another at runtime. A live order queue needs real-time updates. Client-submitted prices could be tampered with. Selling a product should deduct from multiple ingredients, not just one.
groundwork.solution: A shared Zod + tRPC v11 contract across all three apps so schema drift breaks the build. SSE with React Query invalidation for the live queue. Server-side repricing on every order. Recipe-based inventory deduction with low-stock alerts. Built in two days as a full-stack prototype.
results: Full coffee shop stack — ordering, kitchen queue, inventory, loyalty — in one typed codebase
Order queue updates in real time via Server-Sent Events
Server-side repricing eliminates price tampering by design

apex-motors.title: Apex Motors
apex-motors.summary: A full dealership platform — inventory SPA with financing, trade-in, and service booking, backed by an Express API and a JWT admin dashboard managing vehicles, leads, and orders.
apex-motors.overview: A car dealership's web presence is usually a static brochure — visitors can't browse live inventory, filter by price, get a financing pre-qualification, or book a service. The sales team manages vehicles and leads in spreadsheets.
apex-motors.challenge: Inventory lived in spreadsheets with no searchable online catalog. Leads came from scattered phone calls with no triage workflow. Vehicle photos were uploaded unoptimized, bloating the site. There was no purchase-intent flow for visitors ready to commit.
apex-motors.solution: A React SPA with faceted inventory search, financing and trade-in forms, and purchase-intent checkout — backed by an Express 5 + MySQL API with JWT admin dashboard, server-side WebP image pipeline, and a unified leads system funneling four intent types into one triage workflow.
results: Inventory moved from spreadsheets to a live, filterable online catalog
Four lead types consolidated into one pipeline with admin triage
Vehicle photos auto-optimized to WebP on upload

faq.q: How much does a project cost?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the job — how many screens, how many features, and whether you need it on phones too. A small website costs far less than a full product. Tell us what you have in mind and we price it for you.
A first version usually takes a few weeks. A complete product takes longer. We give you a realistic timeline before we begin, and we keep you updated as we go.

faq.q: How many changes can I ask for?
faq.a: Two rounds at each stage — once for the design, once for the build. You look at the work, send all your notes together, and we apply them. If you need more than that, or you want to add something new, we tell you the cost before we start.

faq.q: Do I own the final product?
faq.a: Yes. Once the project is paid, the code, the design, and all the accounts belong to you. Nothing is locked to us.

faq.q: What if I don't know exactly what I want yet?
faq.a: That is normal, and it is where we start. We help you turn a rough idea into a clear plan before anything gets built.
We do not disappear. Any bug you find in the first 30 days, we fix for free. After that we stay available to fix issues, make improvements, and help your product grow.

sections.heading: Agreement to Terms
sections.body: By using this website or working with CUVATEX, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use our services.

sections.heading: Services
sections.body: CUVATEX designs and builds software products — websites, web apps, mobile apps, product design, and custom backend systems. The exact scope of each project is agreed with the client before work starts.

sections.heading: Client Responsibilities
sections.body: Clients agree to give timely feedback, and to provide the content, access, and information needed to complete the work. Delays on the client's side can delay delivery.

sections.heading: Payment Terms
sections.body: Projects are priced with a fixed quote agreed before work starts. Payment is split in two: 50% to begin (the deposit), and 50% when the finished work is handed over. Late payment may pause work until it is resolved.

sections.heading: Revisions
sections.body: Each stage of the project includes two rounds of changes. A round means you review the work and send us your notes once. Extra rounds, or changes that add new features beyond the agreed scope, are quoted separately before we do them.

sections.heading: Bug Fixes After Delivery
sections.body: For 30 days after delivery, we fix any bug in the delivered work at no extra cost. A bug means something we built does not work the way it was agreed. New features, new requests, or problems caused by changes made by someone else are not covered.

sections.heading: Intellectual Property
sections.body: Once a project is paid in full, the client owns the final deliverables. CUVATEX may show completed work in its own portfolio unless the client asks otherwise in writing.

sections.heading: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: CUVATEX works carefully, but is not liable for indirect or incidental damages arising from the use of a delivered product, to the extent allowed by law.

sections.heading: Termination
sections.body: Either party can end an engagement with written notice. The deposit is not refunded, as it reserves the time we set aside for your project. Any work completed beyond the deposit is billed at the agreed rate, and we hand over what is finished.

sections.heading: Governing Law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the laws of Algeria.

sections.heading: Changes to These Terms
sections.body: These terms may be updated from time to time. Continuing to use our services after a change means you accept the updated terms.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about these terms? Reach out through our contact page or by email.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This page explains what information CUVATEX collects through this website, and how it is used.

sections.heading: Information We Collect
sections.body: When you use the contact form, we collect the name, email, and message you provide. We also collect basic, anonymous analytics about how visitors use the site.

sections.heading: How We Use Your Information
sections.body: We use contact form details only to reply to your message. Analytics data is used in aggregate, to understand how the site is used and where it can be improved.

sections.heading: Data Sharing
sections.body: Contact form submissions are processed by Web3Forms, a third-party form-delivery service, in order to deliver your message to us. We do not sell your information to anyone.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body: This site uses Umami, a privacy-friendly analytics tool that does not use cookies and does not track visitors individually.

sections.heading: Data Retention
sections.body: Contact form messages are kept only as long as needed to respond to your inquiry, unless we are required to keep them longer by law.

sections.heading: Your Rights
sections.body: You can ask us to access or delete any information we hold about you by contacting us through the email on our contact page.
